title: 70% of Japanese Think They're Safe from Online Scams
paragraphs: Most people in Japan believe that they would not be tricked by online scams, according to a new survey. However, experts warn that this confidence may be dangerous.

The survey was carried out by LINE Yahoo, the company that runs the popular messaging app LINE. In July 2026, it asked 1,056 LINE users aged 18 to 69 about two types of scams. One is investment scams on social media. The other is "fake police" scams, where criminals pretend to be police officers.

More than 70% of people said they did not think they could be tricked. Older people were more likely to feel this way. The survey also found that about 70% of people knew about fake police scams, but only about 40% knew about investment scams on social media.
However, about half of the people said they had received messages or calls that could lead to fraud. More than 60% of these people did not report it or ask anyone for help.
According to a 2018 survey by Japan's National Police Agency, 78% of real scam victims had also believed that they would not become victims.

Scams are a big problem in Japan. In 2025, there were 9,538 cases of investment fraud on social media, and people lost about 127 billion yen. There were also 10,936 cases of fake police scams, with losses of about 98.5 billion yen.
LINE Yahoo has added features to help protect users. For example, people can report strange messages and block messages from strangers.
